1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Peñaseca for three days. In spring, Lucía Romero’s elder sister had left for Madrid, and ever since then Lucía had been running the village’s small apothecary shop alone.
As night fell, she closed the shutters, counted what she had earned that day, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone knocked hard on the door below. A man’s voice asked, “Is anyone there?”
A young man stood on the threshold, soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in bloodstained cloth. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need you to treat me,” Lobo said quietly. “I can pay. Would three thousand five hundred reals be enough?”
He took a letter wrapped in waxed paper from his coat. “This letter must reach the monastery of San Blas before May 18.”
To Lucía, treating that wound was child’s play, but the letter troubled her.
Even so, she refused his money and only said, “At dawn tomorrow, I’ll take you to the mountain.”
2: At daybreak, they set out. Lucía carried a basket on her back containing bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope, they came across old Tomás Gil, who was chopping firewood. He set down his axe and told them in a low voice that three strangers had asked at the entrance to the village the previous evening about a wounded young man.
“Take the mountain path, Lucía,” Tomás Gil said. “The royal road isn’t safe.” Lucía thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lucía walked ahead, planting her feet firmly with every step. Lobo followed her in silence.
At noon, the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and the roof of the San Blas monastery appeared in the distance. A nun, Sister Inés, waited at the door, ready to receive visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. “The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter.”
Lobo told Lucía, “I owe you my life.” Lucía smiled. “Then, next time you come, fix the apothecary’s roof for me.” Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At dusk, Lucía descended the mountain alone. When she reached home, it was already night; she lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
